abort.ezviz_cloud_account_missing: EZVIZ cloud account missing. Please reconfigure EZVIZ cloud account

error.invalid_mfa: EZVIZ rejected the verification code. Check the newest code and try again.

confirm.description: Enter RTSP credentials for EZVIZ camera {serial} with IP {ip_address}
confirm.title: Discovered EZVIZ Camera

mfa.description: EZVIZ sent a verification code for {username} by e-mail or SMS. Enter it to finish signing in.
mfa.title: Two-step verification

reauth_confirm.description: Enter credentials to reauthenticate to EZVIZ cloud account
reauth_confirm.title: Authentication expired

abort.no_cameras: This account has no cloud-streamed cameras to set a code for.

data_description.ffmpeg_arguments: The RTSP path appended to a camera's address when you add it with the local IP and RTSP password. The default is the EZVIZ/Hikvision sub-stream. Cameras that stream through the EZVIZ cloud — battery cameras and peepholes — ignore this.
data_description.timeout: How long to wait for a reply from the EZVIZ cloud before giving up.

data_description.code: Six capital letters on the camera's label. Leave it empty to remove the stored code.
data_description.serial: Cameras that stream through the EZVIZ cloud, such as battery cameras.

codes.description: Only cameras with video encryption turned on need a code. It decrypts the cloud live stream inside Home Assistant, so it never reaches a browser. Cameras marked ✓ already have one.
codes.title: Verification codes

data.transcode: Re-encode the cloud live stream to H.264

data_description.transcode: Turn it on if the live view of a cloud camera stays black in your browser or in the Home Assistant app. It uses the Home Assistant host's CPU while someone watches.

video.description: Cloud cameras (battery cameras and peepholes) send HEVC (H.265), which many browsers can't play. Re-encoding to H.264 makes the live view play everywhere.
video.title: Video transcoding

data.auto_snapshot: Take a snapshot when a dashboard shows the camera

data_description.auto_snapshot: Lets the EZVIZ Snapshot card take a new picture each time it comes into view (dashboard opened, tab or app back in front). Each picture wakes a battery camera. Buttons and scripts that call capture_picture are not affected.
data_description.snapshot_interval: An automatic snapshot of a camera is skipped if it took a picture less than this long ago, in seconds, however many dashboards ask. 0 takes one on every view.

snapshots.description: Automatic snapshots from the EZVIZ Snapshot card. A camera is woken for each picture, so keep the interval long enough for battery cameras.
snapshots.title: Snapshots

data_description.max_session: How long one live stream of a battery camera may run before it is stopped, in seconds. 0 removes the limit.

stream.description: A battery camera is stopped after this long even if something is still watching, so it can never be left streaming and draining. This is a safety net independent of the card's own stop button.
stream.title: Maximum stream duration

data_description.linger: How long the stream is held open after the last viewer leaves, in seconds, so a quick re-play does not wake the camera again. 0 closes it at once.

release.description: After the last viewer leaves, the cloud stream is held open for this long before the camera is released. A short hold keeps a second play from waking the camera again; 0 releases it immediately.
release.title: Release the camera after

stream_address.title: Stream address for other apps
stream_address.description:
Other apps (go2rtc, Frigate, …) can read each cloud camera from these token-guarded addresses:

```
{addresses}
```

Opening an address wakes the camera, so switch it on for a moment rather than around the clock. The bundled card keeps working even when these are off.

data.stream_enabled: Allow other apps to read the stream

data_description.stream_enabled: Off by default. Turn it on to let other apps (go2rtc, Frigate, …) read these addresses. The bundled card keeps working either way.
data_description.rotate_token: Replace the stream token. Addresses shared before will stop working; the new ones appear here the next time this screen opens.

capture_picture.description: Takes a new picture through the EZVIZ cloud and shows it in the camera's Snapshot image entity. Wakes battery cameras.

automatic.description: Marks an automatic request (the snapshot card coming into view). It is skipped when automatic snapshots are off under Configure → Snapshots, and uses the minimum time set there unless a minimum interval is given.
automatic.name: Automatic

min_interval.description: Skip the capture if this camera took a picture less than this many seconds ago (0 = always capture). Lets dashboards ask for a picture on every visit without waking the camera each time.
min_interval.name: Minimum interval

capture_picture.name: Capture picture

set_alarm_detection_sensibility.description: Changes the sensibility level of the motion detection.

level.description: Sensibility level. 1-6 for type 0 (normal camera), or 1-100 for type 3 (PIR sensor camera).
level.name: Level

type_value.description: Detection type. 0 for normal camera, or 3 for PIR sensor camera.
type_value.name: Type

set_alarm_detection_sensibility.name: Set detection sensibility

wake_device.description: Wakes a camera from sleep mode. Especially useful for battery cameras.
wake_device.name: Wake camera
